archetypes.name: call-site-audit
archetypes.rationale: The plan adds a 4th positional arg to select_failed_agent_stderr_source but does not audit all existing callers in the repo to confirm none pass unexpected positional args that would silently shift.
archetypes.prompt_body: Grep the entire repo for every call to `select_failed_agent_stderr_source` and compare the actual argument count at each call site against what the plan says. Verify that `run-external-agent.sh` is the only caller, and confirm the plan accounts for every call site in both the timeout path and the non-zero-exit path. Check whether any other scripts source `lib-failed-agent-stderr-tail.sh` and call the function directly; if callers exist outside the plan's listed files, flag them as missing update targets. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: variable-name-drift
archetypes.rationale: The plan forwards --stderr-sink using specific variable names ($SIDECAR_LOG, $codex_wrapper_log) but does not verify those exact names exist and are in scope at the call site in each of the three launcher scripts.
archetypes.prompt_body: For each of the three broken launchers (`scripts/launch-codex-implement.sh`, `scripts/lint-fix-loop.sh`, `skills/review-and-fix/scripts/review-and-fix.sh`), read the actual variable declarations and scoping to confirm the names the plan uses (`$SIDECAR_LOG`, `$codex_wrapper_log`) match the real variable names and are in scope at the `run-external-agent.sh` invocation point. A mismatch means the forwarded path is an empty string, silently reverting to the broken fallback behavior without any error signal. Also verify whether `run_codex` in `lint-fix-loop.sh` is a function or inline code, and whether the wrapper log variable is a local or global. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: sink-lifecycle
archetypes.rationale: The plan's [[ -s ]] guard assumes the sink file is populated before select_failed_agent_stderr_source runs, but does not confirm the sink is created/opened before agent launch in each broken lane.
archetypes.prompt_body: For each of the three broken lanes, trace whether the custom sink file (`$SIDECAR_LOG` / `codex.wrapper.log`) is created and opened for writing *before* the `run-external-agent.sh` call, or whether it could be absent if the agent exits immediately without producing stderr. The `-s` test (non-zero size) will fall through to the existing fallback for an absent or empty sink, which is documented as acceptable, but verify the plan's test cases cover the distinct sub-cases: sink file does not exist vs. sink file exists but is empty. Check `test-lib-failed-agent-stderr-tail.sh` assertions to see if both sub-cases are exercised. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
